item.description: A Winter Storm Watch has been issued by the National Weather Service for Schuylkill County and counties south in central Pennsylvania, with heavy snow possible from late Saturday night through Monday afternoon. The watch, issued at 1:40 p.m. Friday, includes Schuylkill, Dauphin, Lebanon, Adams, York, and Lancaster counties.Snow Accumulations Possible Forecasters say total snow accumulations between 4 and 6 inches are possible during the duration of the storm. item.title: PennDOT Announces Blasting Operations on Route 61 Reconstruction Project Between St. Clair and Frackville
item.description: Motorists traveling on Route 61 between St. Clair and Frackville should prepare for brief delays this week due to scheduled blasting operations. According to PennDOT, several short-term traffic stoppages of approximately 15 minutes each will occur in both directions along PA 61 as part of the ongoing Route 61 St. Clair–Frackville Reconstruction Project. item.title: Winter Storm Warning Issued for Schuylkill County; 6–12 Inches of Snow Possible
item.description: The National Weather Service has issued a Winter Storm Warning for Schuylkill County, with significant snowfall and strong winds expected to impact the area Sunday into Monday. The warning is in effect from 5:00 AM Sunday until 1:00 PM EST Monday. What to ExpectForecasters say heavy snow is likely, with total accumulations between 6 and 12 inches possible across Schuylkill County and portions of central Pennsylvania. item.title: Boil Water Advisory Lifted for Shenandoah Area Aqua Customers
item.description: Aqua Pennsylvania has officially lifted the Boil Water Advisory for all customers in the Shenandoah service area, including residents and businesses in Shenandoah Borough, West Mahanoy Township, and Butler Township. According to Aqua Pennsylvania, the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) has reviewed testing results and approved the company’s decision to end the advisory.
